newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian unions oppose any move to cut pensions.
newsitem.headline: Italian unions oppose any move to cut pensions.

text.p: Italian trade union leaders warned the government on Tuesday that they would strongly oppose any move by the government to impose a levy on pension benefits in a planned supplementary budget.

"We are absolutely united in expressing our opposition to making cash withdrawals from the Italian pensions system," Pietro Larizza, secretary general of the UIL labour confederation told a news conference.

The government is preparing to announce a mini-budget in the coming weeks in an effort to keep on course its efforts to bring the ratio of the public sector deficit to gross domestic product to three percent.
Larizza said the unions had not been told by the government what the size of the mini-budget would be. Newspapers have reported it would be of the order of 14 to 15 trillion lire.
Sergio D'Antoni, leader of the CISL trade union confederation, said he would even oppose a levy on pension benefits drawn by people who had retired early.
"That is the worst thing because that means that rules are laid down, people take advantage of them and then they get punished," said D'Antoni.
Sergio Cofferati, leader of Italy's powerful CGIL trade union, and Larizza declined to comment on specific scenarios.
"I am not commenting on anything until the government presents its proposal," said Cofferati.
